claims.claim: **Serious bacterial infection and meningococcal disease are absent in most children with petechiae**, and frequently no cause is identified. ⚠️ **Seriously unwell children with petechiae/purpura need urgent management.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Serious bacterial infection (meningococcal disease included) can present as a non-blanching rash, febrile or afebrile.** Pneumococcal and meningococcal bacteraemia have fallen since routine vaccination.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Petechiae and purpura do not blanch.** Glass test: press a drinking glass firmly on the rash — if it does not disappear, it is non-blanching. **Petechiae are pinpoint; purpura are larger (over 2 mm).**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Every child with petechiae/purpura and fever needs prompt senior clinician review.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Higher-risk history:** under 6 months or incompletely immunised · rapid onset or progression · **prior antibiotics may mask bacterial infection** · immunosuppression or previous invasive bacterial infection.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **The child is unwell if:** abnormal vital signs (tachycardia, tachypnoea, desaturation in air) · **cold shock** (a narrow pulse pressure, cold extremities, prolonged refill) · **warm shock** (bounding pulses, wide pulse pressure, flushed skin, rapid refill) · altered conscious state (inconsolable crying, lethargy) · limb tenderness or difficulty mobilising.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In every child, look for haematological causes:** hepatomegaly or splenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, joint swelling or erythema.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mechanical:** vomiting or coughing (petechiae in the superior vena cava distribution, above the nipples) · local pressure (holding, tight tourniquet) · non-accidental or accidental injury.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Infective:** enterovirus, adenovirus, influenza; *N. meningitidis*, *S. pneumoniae*, *H. influenzae*, group A streptococcus, *S. aureus*.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Haematological and other:** ITP · malignancy including acute leukaemia · aplastic anaemia · DIC · HUS · Henoch-Schönlein purpura · vasculitis · drug-induced thrombocytopenia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Any newborn with petechiae needs prompt senior review** — consider congenital CMV, toxoplasmosis and neonatal lupus as well.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If no senior clinician is available, manage by the flowchart** — the safest approach. Review of a blood film is mandatory to rule out another diagnosis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ceftriaxone 100 mg/kg (max 4 g) IV daily.** ⚠️ Avoid where possible in neonates under 41 weeks' gestation, especially with jaundice or when calcium-containing solutions (TPN included) are running.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cefotaxime 50 mg/kg (max 2 g) IV** — 12-hourly in week 1 of life, 6–8-hourly in weeks 2–4, 6-hourly after week 4.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the paediatric team** for any unwell child including suspected meningococcal disease, diagnostic uncertainty or follow-up, and escalation advice.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when a serious cause is unlikely** on assessment and/or investigations — and **always advise return if the child becomes more unwell.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23
